title: DoorDash Outage Make-Good Ledger
oneLiner: A restaurant and driver make-good tracker for proving lost orders, missed pay, refunds, and customer recovery after a delivery-platform outage.
targetUser: Independent restaurant managers, franchise shift leads, and delivery drivers caught in delivery-app downtime.
keyUX: Start an outage incident, import or mock affected orders, tag customer harm and driver pay gaps, attach screenshots, generate platform support claims, and queue customer make-goods.
sourceSignals: S14 - Restaurant owners discuss platform fee economics: https://www.reddit.com/r/restaurantowners/comments/1hqhark/is_delivery_service_platform_worth_it_sorry_im/
S5 - Delivery fee crackdown / platform pressure: https://www.businessinsider.com/delivery-apps-fee-backlash-federal-regulation-2026-4
stitchPrompt: Create a responsive web app called "DoorDash Outage Make-Good Ledger" for independent restaurant managers, franchise shift leads, and delivery drivers caught in delivery-app downtime. The app is based on observed user pull: restaurants and drivers already save app-error screenshots, watch outage reports, file support tickets, refund angry customers, and try to prove lost orders or missed pay after platform failures. The app should use an incident ledger mechanic around the trigger moment "the delivery app crashes during service" and make the first screen communicate "The app failed, but you still need the receipt." Use the user's own language: "The platform broke, but I need proof before support closes the case." Build the core workflow around outage timestamps, order export, screenshots, POS records, refund status, driver shift records, and customer recovery actions, and produce a compensation packet plus make-good queue. Required sections: outage incident header, affected order ledger, app-error screenshot/status log, driver missed-pay lane, customer refund/make-good queue, POS vs platform mismatch panel, platform support claim builder, and recovery summary card. Emotional pressure to make visible: 자산 방어, customer blame, lost tips/pay, and platform support deadlines. Design direction: use the `field-ops` profile with slate/steel operational panels, strong timestamp hierarchy, rugged mobile-friendly rows, restrained cyan action accents plus amber incident warnings, large tap targets for shift use, and no marketing hero. Avoid generic dashboard framing; make the main interaction feel like a live outage evidence log built during a messy dinner rush.
